newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown details Treasury team duties.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown details Treasury team duties.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown has allocated reponsibilities to his ministerial team, the Treasury said on Friday.

-- Chief Secretary to the Treasury ALISTAIR DARLING will take charge of public expenditure planning and control. He will look at value for money in the public services and institute a comprehensive spending reviews.

Darling will oversee public sector pay, including parliamentary pay, allowances and superannuation. He will also take a strategic overview of the financial system and financial services as well as export credit and the financial aspects of devolution.

-- Paymaster General GEOFFREY ROBINSON will have responsibility for the Enterprise and Growth Unit. He will oversee issues concerning the windfall levy on privatised utilities and the Welfare-to-Work scheme that tax will fund.

Additionally, Robinson will be in charge of Public/Private Partnerships, competition and deregulation policy and a review of corporation tax. He will assist Darling on public expenditure planning and control and will oversee Treasury interests in small firms and general accounting issues.

-- Financial Secretary DAWN PRIMAROLO will oversee the Inland Revenue, Customs and Excise and Valuation Office Agency. That will include taking responsiblity for Inland Revenue taxes (except the windfall levy), Customs and Excise duties and taxes, and charities. She will look at energy efficiency related to the environment and take charge of parliamentary financial business.

-- Economic Secretary HELEN LIDDELL will have responsibility for the financial system and financial services as well as the Department of National Savings, National Investment and Loan Office and for the Treasury's interests as shareholder of the Bank of England. She will oversee foreign exchange reserves management, debt management policy and the annual borrowing programme.

She will also have a brief to watch international financial and monetary issues and institutions as well as the European Commission Budget, reform of the Common Agricultural Policy and future financing. She will look at matters surrounding European economic and monetary union in support of the Chancellor.

Liddell will be in charge of the Office for National Statistics, Royal Mint and the Government's Actuary's Department and will help Darling on the tax and Finance Bill. She will brief parliament on the economy and statistics and take responsibility for low pay and the minimum wage and women's issues.

Minister for Trade and Competitiveness in Europe Lord DAVID SIMON has a place in both the Treasury and Department of Trade and Industry. He will chair the Interdepartmental taskforce on competitiveness in Europe and sit on the Economic and European Cabinet Committees, and the Taskforce for the British Presidency. Britain will hold the presidency of the European Union in the first half of 1998. He will also carry out ad hoc projects for the Chancellor on economic issues.
